This means either the whole graph holds very few LHC-black-hole-related claims, or the result cap (k=2) is truncating the candidate list. Expected: several results per query per the tool description ("top matches... above a low floor"). A cap this low weakens the retrieval side of identity matching: a true counterpart could sit in third place and never surface, and I cannot distinguish 'novel' from 'below the cutoff'. Proposal: raise the default result count returned to something like 5-10, or document the cap so matchers know to interpret a 2-result response as possibly truncated.

input.reasoning: Searched eleven framings across five turns: the claim as written, the proposed canonical form, paraphrase families (threshold/Planck-scale phrasings, SM-attribution phrasings), the flat negation ("No black holes will be formed..."), the contrary capability claims ("The LHC could create microscopic black holes", "LHC energies are high enough..."), the stronger existential contrary ("The LHC has actually produced microscopic black holes"), and the experimental-null phrasing. The same two candidates surfaced every time at only moderate similarity, and no dedicated node for black hole production at the LHC appeared under any framing, including the negation probes, so the graph appears to hold neither this claim nor its counterpart. Neither candidate is the same proposition: "Collisions at the LHC present no danger" is the broad safety conclusion, and the two come apart (collisions could create a black hole yet present no danger via Hawking evaporation, or create none yet present danger another way), so different considerations bear on them; the cosmic-ray claim is a separate, independent argument in the same safety debate. The source sentence, read for fidelity, asserts the world-level impossibility with the Standard Model as warrant, not a conditional proposition about what the theory predicts, so the SM attribution stays in the instance text and the claim is the capability question. Direction chosen on the discourse's own terms: the positive, named thesis (microscopic black hole production at the LHC) over its negation-flavored form ("too low to create"), per the affirmative-form rule; this instance therefore records as denying. Confidence held below 0.8 because every query returned at most two results (reported separately as issue bd224d59-ea12-42ad-9769-3991083e8121), so a closer counterpart could in principle sit below the cutoff; the consistency of the same two neighbors across all framings is the main reason to think the neighborhood really is just these two.
input.direction_note: The affirmative capability thesis is what the discourse actually debates and searches for (microscopic black hole production at the LHC, hypothesized under TeV-scale gravity/large extra dimensions), so the canonical form states that thesis; Standard Model reassurances like this source land on the denying side, which is recorded as instance_stance "denies" rather than fixed by inverting the form.

"Natural cosmic-ray collisions on Earth have already produced the equivalent of the LHC's entire experimental program" (ea8dd956-8fc0-4780-94c1-541ac1f71345) is an independent argument in the same safety debate and a distinct proposition. The speculative counterpart thesis (production possible under large extra dimensions) is the affirming side of this same node, not a separate claim.
